acceptance_criteria.criterion: When the Discover page loads, the system shall render a tagline element with text "Live conditions for Vancouver's 9 best beaches" as the first visible content element within the page body.
acceptance_criteria.test_assertion_template: expect(screen.getByText("Live conditions for Vancouver's 9 best beaches")).toBeVisible()

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When the Discover page loads with weather data available, each beach list row shall display a color-coded verdict badge showing one of "Perfect", "Good", "Fair", or "Skip" derived from the computeVerdict utility.
When weather data is loading, each beach list row shall display a skeleton placeholder in place of the verdict badge.
When the user taps the "Map" toggle button, the system shall replace the beach list with the interactive map component, and the toggle shall indicate "Map" as the active view.
When the user taps the "List" toggle button while in map view, the system shall replace the map with the beach list, and the toggle shall indicate "List" as the active view.

When the Discover page renders beach list rows, each row shall contain exactly: the beach name, a verdict badge, and the current temperature. No tagline, vibe icons, thumbnail image, or water quality dot shall be present in the row.
While the viewport width is less than 640px, the beach detail hero section shall have a maximum height of 150px, ensuring the verdict card is visible without scrolling.

When the user is viewing a beach detail page, the system shall display previous and next navigation controls showing the adjacent beach names (with directional chevron icons) that link to the adjacent beaches in alphabetical order.
If the current beach is the first alphabetically, the "Previous" button shall wrap to the last beach. If the current beach is the last, the "Next" button shall wrap to the first.
acceptance_criteria.test_assertion_template: // render first-alpha beach; expect(prevLink.getAttribute('href')).toContain(lastAlphaBeach.id); // render last-alpha beach; expect(nextLink.getAttribute('href')).toContain(firstAlphaBeach.id)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When water quality data is available on the beach detail conditions grid, the system shall display the water quality level as a text label ("Safe", "Advisory", "Closed", "Off-Season", "Unknown") with a colored background matching the severity (green, amber, red, gray, gray respectively).

When a beach detail page loads, the About tab shall display a "Similar vibes" section showing up to 3 other beaches that share at least one vibe with the current beach, each linking to that beach's detail page.
When the user taps the dark mode toggle in the header, the system shall apply the `dark` class to the document root and persist the preference to localStorage.
When the app loads, the system shall read the stored theme preference from localStorage and apply it. If no preference is stored, the system shall default to light mode.
The system shall not have a `/compare` route. Navigating to `/compare` shall redirect to `/discover` via the catch-all route.
When a weather API call fails, the system shall display an error card with the message "Couldn't load conditions" and a "Try again" button that re-triggers the API call.
acceptance_criteria.test_assertion_template: mockFetchError('/api/weather/english-bay'); expect(await screen.findByText("Couldn't load conditions")).toBeInTheDocument(); expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Try again' })).toBeInTheDocument()

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When a tide API call fails, the tide section shall display "Tide data unavailable" with a retry button.
acceptance_criteria.test_assertion_template: mockFetchError('/api/tides/english-bay'); expect(await screen.findByText('Tide data unavailable')).toBeInTheDocument(); expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Try again' })).toBeInTheDocument()

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When weather data loads successfully, the conditions section shall display a "Last updated" timestamp showing the relative time (e.g., "Updated 5 min ago") derived from the API response timestamp.
The Discover page shall not render vibe filter chip buttons. The "What's your vibe?" heading and associated filter UI shall be removed.
When the beaches API call fails on the Discover page, the system shall display an error card with the message "Couldn't load beaches" and a "Try again" button that re-triggers the API call.
acceptance_criteria.test_assertion_template: mockFetchError('/api/beaches'); expect(await screen.findByText("Couldn't load beaches")).toBeInTheDocument(); expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Try again' })).toBeInTheDocument()

interface_locations: TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md:### 13. Remove Vibe Filters from Discover

non_scope: No changes to the color palette, typography, or design tokens
No changes to the Tailwind config
No backend API changes (functions/ or worker/)
No changes to PWA/service worker configuration
No changes to TideCanvas, BeachMap, WeatherForecast, ActivityRecommendations, or SunTimesWidget components
testing_strategy: Unit tests for VerdictBadge (each recommendation level), computeSummaryVerdict logic, SimilarVibes (correct matches), BeachNavigation (wrap-around), ErrorState (message + retry callback). Integration tests for Discover page (tagline present, verdict badges, list/map toggle, vibe filter absence), beach detail hero height at 375px viewport. E2E for dark mode toggle persistence across navigation. Visual regression check for dark: class Tailwind variants.
